# Reading library {.unnumbered}

Use official links rather than uploaded copies. Access notes distinguish a publisher record from an identified free full-text route; institutional entitlement is not guaranteed.

## Meeting 1: Is there a scientific method?

**@platt1964.** [Strong Inference](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.146.3642.347). Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@cleland2002.** [Methodological and Epistemic Differences between Historical Science and Experimental Science](https://doi.org/10.1086/342455). Philosophy of Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 2: Exploratory experimentation is not theory-free

**@steinle1997.** [Entering New Fields: Exploratory Uses of Experimentation](https://doi.org/10.1086/392587). Philosophy of Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@karaca2013.** [The Strong and Weak Senses of Theory-Ladenness of Experimentation: Theory-Driven versus Exploratory Experiments in the History of High-Energy Particle Physics](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0269889712000300). Science in Context. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 3: From coastal traces to earthquake histories

**@atwater1987.** [Evidence for great Holocene earthquakes along the outer coast of Washington state](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70014720). Science. USGS publication record with publisher link.

**@nelson1996.** [Identifying coseismic subsidence in tidal-wetland stratigraphic sequences at the Cascadia subduction zone of western North America](https://doi.org/10.1029/95JB01051). Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 4: Plate tectonics: concept formation and a discriminating test

**@wilson1965.** [A New Class of Faults and their Bearing on Continental Drift](https://doi.org/10.1038/207343a0). Nature. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@sykes1967.** [Mechanism of earthquakes and nature of faulting on the mid-oceanic ridges](https://doi.org/10.1029/JZ072i008p02131). Journal of Geophysical Research. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 5: New sensing capability versus trustworthy measurement

**@lindsey2019.** [Illuminating seafloor faults and ocean dynamics with dark fiber distributed acoustic sensing](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aay5881). Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@lindsey2020.** [On the Broadband Instrument Response of Fiber-Optic DAS Arrays](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2019JB018145). Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth. Publisher full-text page.

## Meeting 6: Explore freely; distinguish exploration from confirmation

**@tukey1962.** [The Future of Data Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177704711). The Annals of Mathematical Statistics. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@nosek2018.** [The preregistration revolution](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856500/). Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Free full text in PubMed Central.

## Meeting 7: Field and marine research under real constraints

**@powell2007.** [The Rigours of an Arctic Experiment: The Precarious Authority of Field Practices in the Canadian High Arctic, 1958--1970](https://doi.org/10.1068/a38294). Environment and Planning A. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@becker2019.** [Fifty Years of Scientific Ocean Drilling](https://tos.org/oceanography/article/fifty-years-of-scientific-ocean-drilling). Oceanography. Free publisher article and PDF link.

## Meeting 8: Serendipity, anomaly, and scientific interestingness

**@moore2025.** [The Serendipity of Discovery: Life of a Geochemist](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-marine-050823-103645). Annual Review of Marine Science. Open-access publisher article; CC BY 4.0.

**@yaqub2018.** [Serendipity: Towards a taxonomy and a theory](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048733317301774). Research Policy. Open-access publisher article.

## Meeting 9: Hypothesis testing when several models fit

**@oreskes1994.** [Verification, Validation, and Confirmation of Numerical Models in the Earth Sciences](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.263.5147.641). Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@beven2001.** [Equifinality, data assimilation, and uncertainty estimation in mechanistic modelling of complex environmental systems using the GLUE methodology](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0022-1694(01)00421-8). Journal of Hydrology. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 10: Scientific novelty: new to whom, compared with what?

**@uzzi2013.** [Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1240474). Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@fontana2020.** [New and atypical combinations: An assessment of novelty and interdisciplinarity](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.respol.2020.104063). Research Policy. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 11: Scientific advance: cumulative work and field-shaping change

**@wu2019.** [Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-0941-9). Nature. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@petersen2025.** [The disruption index suffers from citation inflation: Re-analysis of temporal CD trend and relationship with team size reveal discrepancies](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1751157724001172). Journal of Informetrics. Open-access journal article; use the 2025 version of record.

## Meeting 12: Scientific polymathy: breadth, specialization, and borrowed competence

**@burke2020.** [The Polymath: A Cultural History from Leonardo da Vinci to Susan Sontag](https://yalebooks.yale.edu/book/9780300250022/the-polymath/). Yale University Press. Publisher and [JSTOR](https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctv15pjzh6) records; not open access. Use library reserve procedures for any chapter scan.

**@kitcher1990.** [The Division of Cognitive Labor](https://doi.org/10.2307/2026796). The Journal of Philosophy. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Meeting 13: What architecture follows from practice, and what would show it worked?

**@boiko2023.** [Autonomous chemical research with large language models](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06792-0). Nature. Open-access publisher article.

**@chen2025.** [ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/f12b4df26344f3be803c06b555252efe-Abstract-Conference.html). International Conference on Learning Representations. Open conference proceedings with paper PDF and review links; no DOI invented.

Discussant-led for this meeting:

**@messeri2024.** [Artificial intelligence and illusions of understanding in scientific research](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07146-0). Nature. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@flake2020.** [Measurement Schmeasurement: Questionable Measurement Practices and How to Avoid Them](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515245920952393). Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

## Optional extensions

**@boudreau2016.** [Looking Across and Looking Beyond the Knowledge Frontier: Intellectual Distance, Novelty, and Resource Allocation in Science](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2015.2285). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@novbench2026.** [NovBench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Academic Paper Novelty Assessment](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1607/). Open ACL Anthology proceedings with PDF and BibTeX.

**@shibayama2021.** [Measuring novelty in science with word embedding](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0254034). Open access; consult the linked 2026 correction to Table 4.

**@machado2026.** [Generative AI bias against scientific novelty: a cautionary tale from a small-sample evaluation of research proposals](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11192-026-05792-x). Publisher article; the experiment concerns one funder, year, and model configuration.

**@dellsen2016.** [Scientific progress: Knowledge versus understanding](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.shpsa.2016.01.003). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@azoulay2019.** [Does Science Advance One Funeral at a Time?](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20161574). Publisher offers complimentary full-text PDF.

**@wang2017.** [Bias against novelty in science: A cautionary tale for users of bibliometric indicators](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.respol.2017.06.006). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@hardwig1991.** [The Role of Trust in Knowledge](https://doi.org/10.2307/2027007). The Journal of Philosophy. Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

**@wright2025.** [What and Whose Knowledge? Measuring Epistemic Diversity in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04226). arXiv. Open preprint; not peer reviewed at the time of listing.

**@rassenfosse2022.** [Scientific rewards for biomedical specialization are large and persistent](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-022-01400-5). BMC Biology. Open access (CC BY).

**@messick1995.** [Validity of psychological assessment: Validation of inferences from persons’ responses and performances as scientific inquiry into score meaning](https://doi.org/10.1037/0003-066X.50.9.741). Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.

[Correction to Shibayama et al., Table 4 (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0341474).

## Beyond the syllabus

Systems and benchmarks rather than papers are catalogued separately in [prior art](prior-art.qmd). Readings the group adds during the quarter go in [suggested readings](suggested-readings.qmd).
